claims.text: The target is a high-performance refractory material in the solid state near its melting point.
Well-tempered metadynamics within DFT-based molecular dynamics accelerates sampling of the solid-liquid phase transition.
The proposed method enables efficient determination of melting temperature.
The proposed method enables accurate determination of melting temperature.
The proposed method enables determination of entropy and enthalpy of fusion.
The proposed method enables determination of volume change at the melting point.
The simulations should be performed near the melting point under conditions in which solid and liquid phases coexist.
A structural or coordination-number-based order parameter can distinguish the solid and liquid phases.
The metadynamics bias lowers the effective free-energy barriers between solid and liquid states.
Lowering the effective free-energy barriers accelerates sampling of solid-liquid transitions.
Accelerated transition sampling produces faster convergence of free-energy estimates.
The converged free-energy estimates allow extraction of the stated melting properties.
The method significantly reduces computational cost relative to full thermodynamic integration using ab initio molecular dynamics.
Full thermodynamic integration using unbiased DFT-based molecular dynamics provides accurate melting-property calculations.
Full thermodynamic integration using unbiased DFT-based molecular dynamics is computationally prohibitive for high-throughput screening.
The proposed approach may be less effective for materials with complex or multiple competing phase transitions when the order parameter omits relevant structural changes.
The accuracy and efficiency of the method depend on tuning the bias deposition frequency, Gaussian height and width, and bias factor.
Optimal metadynamics parameters may vary with material complexity.
